newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt pound almost stable despite dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Egypt pound almost stable despite dlr demand.

text.p: The Egyptian pound's average bid rate against the dollar was up while that for the offered rate went down in the private-sector market on Wednesday among strong demand for the U.S. currency, bankers said.
The bankers say the dollar is in demand by public sector banks ahead of the end of the financial year on June 30 and by foreign mutual funds.
"The funds are buying dollars in small quantities so that it does not go up," one banker said.
"Their pound deposits declined sharply," he added. The funds' move has been attributed to the weak stock market.
Private-sector bankers said the dollar ranged from 3.3940 pounds to 3.3960 pounds bid and from 3.3975 pounds to 3.3990 offered in the interbank market.
A survey of five actively trading banks gave average rates of 3.3950 pounds bid and 3.3981 offered. The averages compare to 3.3960 pounds bid and 3.3979 pounds offered on Tuesday.
The Central Bank calculated the average exchange rate at midday as 3.392138 buy and 3.398121 sell.
